predecessors.name: Novgorod Republic
predecessors.text: the Pskov core (Pskov, Izborsk, Gdov, Ostrov, Pechory), which Cliopatria's Novgorod shape of 1236-1240 contains (107 of its 108 cells)

successors.name: Grand Principality of Moscow
successors.text: the Pskov land: the Pskov Republic 'annexed' by Vasily III in 1510

ledger.x: 1285: Pskov stands apart from Novgorod, as Cliopatria draws it.
1348: the Treaty of Bolotovo recognises Pskov's independence from Novgorod; Pskov becomes the Pskov Republic.
1422: two fringe cells (now in Estonia and Latvia) pass to the Livonian Conference.
January 1510: the Pskov Republic ends, annexed by Vasily III.

wars.name: Livonian siege of Pskov (1299)
wars.outcome: 'On 4 March 1299, the Livonian Order unexpectedly invaded north-western Russia and laid siege to Pskov'; Dovmont defeated them again after a battle on the Velikaya River and died on 20 May 1299 in a plague.

wars.name: Lithuanian-Muscovite border war over Pskov
wars.outcome: 'Lithuania attacks Pskov, and Moscow sends troops, starting a border war that lasts until 1408'; no territorial result on the page.

wars.name: Muscovite-Livonian war of 1501-1503
wars.outcome: Pskov and Moscow forces lost the Battle of the Siritsa River to the Livonian Order in 1501; a six-year truce followed in summer 1503.

wars.name: Moscow's annexation of Pskov
wars.outcome: Vasily III, in Novgorod in 1509, summoned Pskov's representatives, accused the Pskovites at Epiphany 1510, had the veche bell removed on 13 January and entered Pskov on 24 January 1510; Pskov was annexed without battle.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary: the Pskov page names only neighbours (Novgorod, Lithuania, the Livonian Order) and a 1417 peace treaty with the Order, and the 1503 truce, without lines.
